author: human
request:
Feature request: visits can currently only be created, never corrected. Two
product decisions come with it, made here as the product owner:

- Non-goal NG-5 is narrowed: cancelling a booked visit stays out of scope,
  but correcting its date and description is now in. Record the narrowing
  the way the project records non-goal changes.
- The edit form is reachable by its URL alone: the owner detail page gains
  no edit link in this request. A visible entry point may come as a
  follow-up request.

Add editing for a booked visit:

- GET /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit shows the visit
  form prefilled with that visit's current date and description. Reuse the
  existing visit form template (pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm) and its `visit`
  model attribute.
- POST to the same URL validates like visit creation (description required,
  date in the future). On success it updates that visit in place — the pet
  must not gain an additional visit record — and redirects to the owner
  detail page. On validation failure it redisplays the form.

Cover the new behavior with tests.

These are all the product decisions; no further product answer will come
during the work. Where a choice still seems open, take the narrowest reading
consistent with this request and record the open question rather than
waiting.

  follow-up request.

author: product-requirements-expert
title: Visit corrections
summary: A booked visit's date and description can be corrected. The correction form opens prefilled with what is recorded, is held to the booking rules, and an accepted correction changes that visit in place rather than adding another.
acceptance_criteria: given a booked visit, when its correction form is opened, then the form shows that visit's recorded date and description
given a booked visit, when a description and a future date are submitted, then that visit carries the new date and description, and the owner's record is shown
given a pet with one booked visit, when a correction is accepted, then the pet still has one visit
given a blank description, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the form is shown again, and the description is named
given a date of today or earlier, when the correction is submitted, then it is refused, the form is shown again, and the date is named
non_goals: cancelling or withdrawing a booked visit (NG-5)
a link to the correction form from the owner's record — deferred by owner decision, recorded as an open question
correcting anything on a visit beyond its date and description
notes: Four questions the intake left unstated are recorded in the PRD's Open Questions at the narrowest reading, per the owner's standing instruction: the missing entry point, the date rule's effect on an already-past visit, whether the correction form shows the pet's other visits, and whether a mismatched owner or pet path is refused. REQ-VISITEDIT-001 claims nothing on the last two. The intake record at handoff line 1 states the owner's preference on reusing the existing booking form; mechanism is the design stage's call. docs/adr/README.md needs an index row for the new non-goal ADR — that file is outside product write scope.

author: system-design-expert
architectural_fit: Correction reuses the create-or-edit controller shape PetController already runs, with one small adjustment. PetController resolves its form-backing object through a single @ModelAttribute whose petId path variable is declared optional (PetController.java:75-87, read directly; no IDE oracle connected, so this is the weaker read-based basis rather than a symbol resolution). VisitController's loadPetWithVisit takes the same adjustment: an optional visitId path variable selects the recorded Visit instead of constructing a new one, and pet.addVisit is skipped on that branch. GET and POST on /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit then reuse the existing view name and the existing date rule verbatim. The adjustment is a new Pet.getVisit(Integer) lookup mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer) (Owner.java:117-127); it keeps visit resolution inside the aggregate, which system-design Contracts already records as the owner-feature invariant. No new type, package, dependency, or ADR: the scope decision is already carried by docs/adr/2026-08-15-non-goal-visit-cancellation.md, and docs/adr/README.md gained its index row in this dispatch.
integration_points: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit gains @PathVariable(name="visitId", required=false) Integer visitId; the new-visit branch is unchanged for the two existing /visits/new routes
Pet gains a getVisit(Integer) accessor returning the recorded Visit or null, mirroring Owner.getPet(Integer)
Write path stays owners.save(owner) with cascade from the Owner aggregate root; no VisitRepository is introduced
The correction POST redirects to redirect:/owners/{ownerId} and refuses by returning pets/createOrUpdateVisitForm, matching processNewVisitForm

createOrUpdateVisitForm.html already branches on ${visit['new']} for its heading and the previous-visits table, and its form posts to the current URL with no action attribute; prefill follows from the model attribute with no template change required

patterns.description: optional path variable on a shared @ModelAttribute selects new-or-existing form object; the create and edit routes then share one binder and one view
GET/POST pair on /{id}/edit alongside the /new pair in the same controller
lookup-by-identity accessor on the aggregate that skips unpersisted children; Pet.getVisit mirrors it
the non-future date rule, rejected as field error typeMismatch.visitDate; the correction reuses it unchanged

risks.risk: Constructing a fresh Visit on the correction path would add a second element to Pet's LinkedHashSet, since Visit inherits identity equality from BaseEntity and overrides neither equals nor hashCode. That breaks the acceptance criterion that the pet still has one visit.
risks.mitigation: The correction branch returns the instance already held in pet.getVisits() and never calls pet.addVisit. Form binding then mutates that instance in place and owners.save(owner) cascades an update. The acceptance test asserts the visit count on the owner the mocked repository returns.

risks.risk: A visitId belonging to another pet or owner could reach a visit outside the addressed aggregate if the lookup went to the repository by identifier.
risks.mitigation: Resolve strictly through owner.getPet(petId).getVisit(visitId). A mismatch yields null, which fails closed the way loadPetWithVisit already fails on a missing pet — IllegalArgumentException, not a silent edit. This is the trust-boundary placement for the new path variables; the PRD claims nothing about the response shape, so the existing failure behavior is reused rather than a new one invented.

risks.risk: Changing the submit button label to distinguish correction from booking would introduce a message key that all eleven bundles under src/main/resources/messages must carry, or the REQ-LANG-002 bundle-parity test fails.
risks.mitigation: No requirement claims the button label. Leave #{addVisit} in place for this slice. If a label change is wanted later, it is its own slice with the eleven bundle edits.

risks.risk: The existing @InitBinder disallows id and *.id for the whole controller, so a submitted id can never override the path variable.
risks.mitigation: Leave the binder untouched; it already covers the correction routes and holds the mass-assignment mitigation the threat model records.

notes: Five-signal foundational check clean: system-design.md is populated and partly confirmed, ADRs record platform and architecture shape, ubiquitous-language carries Visit, and this slice introduces no bounded context and touches no unrecorded project-level concern. No conflict: the 2026-08-08 non-goal ADR set an explicit reopening condition and the 2026-08-15 ADR meets it, naming REQ-VISITEDIT-001. No design-doc-autofix records exist in the log, so the autofix audit is a no-op. Durable-memory writes this dispatch: docs/adr/README.md index row for the 2026-08-15 non-goal ADR (flagged in the prd-entry as outside product write scope); docs/system-design.md Contracts rows for VisitController, Pet, Visit, and OwnerRepository, plus one invariant sentence recording that a Visit is reached by walking owner to pet to visit. Vocabulary note for prose: ubiquitous-language lists Booking under Avoid as a name for the Visit; use Visit and correction, and keep booked only as the participle the PRD uses. The two PRD open questions this slice does not claim — whether the correction form shows the pet's other visits, and whether a mismatched owner or pet path is refused — are answered incidentally by reusing the existing template and the existing failure path; neither answer is asserted as a requirement and neither needs a test.

author: security-reviewer
recommendations: Surface widening is documented, not silent: two new routes (GET and POST /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit) are recorded in docs/prd.md REQ-VISITEDIT-001 and in the VisitController row of docs/system-design.md. They are state-mutating and unauthenticated, but that is the recorded baseline of this demonstration application (docs/security-principles.md 'What this application is, and what that does not excuse'; docs/system-design.md Security Context) and is not raised as a defect. The change does not leave the application weaker than that baseline.

Supply chain: not verified against the NVD in this review. build.gradle is unchanged and the change adds no dependency; the OWASP dependency-check plugin is not configured in this project, so no NVD match ran here. A human or CI still owns the periodic framework-CVE check for Spring Boot and Jackson.

Note for a future round, no action now: processUpdateVisitForm binds @ModelAttribute Owner and then saves it, so request parameters can write owner fields through the visit-correction endpoint. This is identical to the pre-existing processNewVisitForm shape and carries no privilege gain in an application with no authentication, so it is baseline rather than a regression. If authentication is ever added, both handlers need the owner narrowed to a non-bound lookup at the same time.
approved_aspects: IDOR closed by construction: the corrected visit is resolved by walking owner -> pet -> visit (VisitController.loadPetWithVisit lines 85-92 calling the new Pet.getVisit), so a visitId belonging to another pet or owner never resolves and the handler never trusts the path identifier alone. This satisfies the 'Trusting cross-request state' row of docs/security-principles.md - each request re-resolves the entity it acts on.

Mass assignment control present on the new endpoints: the class-level @InitBinder (VisitController:53-56) disallows 'id' and '*.id' and applies to every handler in the controller, including the two new /visits/{visitId}/edit mappings. The identifier-binding case named in the security brief is therefore closed by default rather than remembered per-endpoint.

Pattern consistency: Pet.getVisit(Integer) mirrors Owner.getPet(Integer) exactly - same isNew() guard, same Objects.equals comparison, same null return contract. No divergent implementation of the same lookup concern was introduced.

No new dangerous surface: the changed production files contain no Runtime/ProcessBuilder/exec, no file or path handling, no serialization or Jackson polymorphic configuration, no string-concatenated query text, and no logging. Persistence stays on the Spring Data JPA repository write path.

Error messages leak nothing: the new IllegalArgumentException carries only the two integer path variables (both parsed by Spring, so non-numeric input never reaches the message). No credential, connection string, or session value can reach the error page through it, which matters because the error page renders the exception message.
Output escaping unchanged: no template was modified, the corrected date and description round-trip through Thymeleaf field binding with default escaping on, and nothing disables it.

Validation re-applied on the correction path: rejectDateNotInTheFuture is shared by booking and correction, so the extracted helper cannot drift between the two, and bean validation (@Valid) still covers the required description.

author: test-reviewer

findings.description: The design-block's own risk analysis (handoff line 9) names the visitId-mismatch path as the trust-boundary mitigation for this slice: loadPetWithVisit now resolves strictly through owner.getPet(petId).getVisit(visitId) and throws IllegalArgumentException when that lookup returns null, closing off reaching a visit outside the addressed aggregate. No test exercises this branch. jacoco confirms the gap: VisitController.loadPetWithVisit shows 2 missed lines (the throw and its message-building line) and Pet.getVisit shows a missed branch (the not-found path returning null) in build/reports/jacoco/test/jacocoTestReport.xml. This is exactly the class of case § Boundary Testing and § Input Validation Testing call for (out-of-range identifier at a trust boundary), and it is new code introduced by this slice, not pre-existing debt.
findings.fix: Add a test (e.g. theVisitCorrectionShouldFailWhenTheVisitIdDoesNotBelongToThePet) that performs GET (or POST) on /owners/{ownerId}/pets/{petId}/visits/{visitId}/edit with a visitId not present on the pet's visit collection, and asserts the resulting error — MockMvc's default unwrapped-exception behavior, or wrap in assertThatThrownBy if the controller's exception propagates past MockMvc in this test setup.

findings.description: Both tests assert on `bookedVisit()`/`owner.getPet(...).getVisits()`, reached through the same Owner instance the mocked repository returns from findById. Spring's @ModelAttribute resolution finds "visit" and "owner" already in the model (put there by loadPetWithVisit) and binds request parameters onto those same object references directly — mutation happens before, and independent of, whether processUpdateVisitForm's `this.owners.save(owner)` call ever executes. A regression that dropped the save() call (the design's own risk mitigation for the in-place-update acceptance criterion) would leave both tests green. Neither test currently pins the persistence call that the acceptance criteria and the design's stated mitigation both depend on.
findings.fix: Add `verify(this.owners).save(this.owner)` (or an ArgumentCaptor assertion on the saved instance) to at least theCorrectedVisitShouldCarryTheNewDateAndDescription, following the tested-as-spec principle that the interaction is the contract at this system boundary (the mocked repository stands in for persistence, which no other assertion in this test observes).

approved_aspects: Test names follow the theSubjectShouldOutcome BDD school and match the PRD's test_names verbatim
Three-tier data naming is clean: BOOKED_DATE/BOOKED_DESCRIPTION/CORRECTED_DATE/CORRECTED_DESCRIPTION/NOT_FUTURE_DATE/BLANK_DESCRIPTION are all role-named, no mystery literals
Construction goes through createAnOwnerWithABookedVisit/createABookedVisit factories rather than raw constructors inline in test bodies
Four-phase structure held with blank-line separation between Act and Assert in every new test
AssertJ used throughout the new assertions (assertThat().returns().returns(), hasSize) with no JUnit-style assertEquals
All five PRD acceptance criteria for REQ-VISITEDIT-001 have a dedicated test, and ./gradlew test passes

author: change-grader

blast_radius.note: Eight files in one module, 31 hunks, no sensitive or build paths; production change is confined to two new routes plus an optional path variable in VisitController and one lookup accessor on Pet, with the two existing /visits/new routes untouched.

semantic_surprise.note: The correction POST binds @ModelAttribute Owner from request parameters and then saves it, so owner fields are writable through the new endpoint (identical to the booking POST, so duplicated rather than introduced), and the reused template still labels the submit button 'Add Visit' and now lists the visit being corrected in its 'Previous Visits' table - user-visible effects that appear in no hunk.

test_adequacy.note: Tests drive the real MVC dispatch and assert outcomes that would fail against a broken implementation: the visit count pins the phantom-visit risk, verify(save) pins persistence, both refusal paths assert the named field error, and PetTests pins getVisit identity and the unsaved-visit exclusion.

reviewer_hedging.note: All four roster reviewers approved with no findings, but the round-2 approvals park recommendations: security carries forward the owner mass-assignment note with a conditional action item should authentication ever be added, plus an unrun supply-chain check, and code-quality carries forward null-versus-Optional on Pet.getVisit.

scope_deviation.note: Zero consultations and zero build retries; the one design revision was a bookkeeping supersession declaring a path, not a scope move, and the NG-5 narrowing that admits this requirement rests on a verbatim recorded owner decision and its own ADR, with the missing entry-point link recorded as deliberately deferred.

rationale: Correction reuses the owner-to-pet-to-visit walk and mutates the recorded visit in place; the logic is sound and genuinely tested. Before merging, open the correction form once - it still reads 'Add Visit' and relists the visit under Previous Visits - and note its POST can write owner fields, as booking already does.
